forward_patch:

+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M7D75MMFBRTFTF72Y6RAE39K
+- 01M7D76AZGGHW3SWFMPS4WZVS2
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8480'
+title: 'Add the RankingBenchmark runner: compare retrieval, selection and decision tiers on the labeled fixture'
+---
+## What
+
+Add the code that runs each tier configuration over `BenchmarkCatalog` and `BenchmarkIntents`, and writes one `BenchmarkReport`.
+
+Files:
+- `Benchmarks/Package.swift`: add the packages FoundationModelsExtras (core product) and FoundationModelsDecision (`FoundationModelsDecisionPooled` product), with the same SSH URLs and `branch: "main"` as the root manifest. Add executable target `RankingBenchmark`.
+- `Benchmarks/Sources/BenchmarkSupport/BenchmarkConfiguration.swift`: `struct BenchmarkConfiguration { let name: String; let makeSearcher: @Sendable ([BenchmarkItem]) -> MetadataSearcher<BenchmarkItem> }`. All configurations use the same `limit` (5) and the same intents.
+- `Benchmarks/Sources/BenchmarkSupport/BenchmarkRunner.swift`: `static func run(_ configurations: [BenchmarkConfiguration], intents: [LabeledIntent], catalog: [BenchmarkItem], repeats: Int) async -> BenchmarkReport`. For each configuration: build one searcher, do one warm-up search and record its duration apart (it loads the models and embeds the catalog), then search each intent `repeats` times and record the ranked ids and the duration of each search. An error of one search counts as an empty result and as one error in the report; the run continues.
+- `Benchmarks/Sources/RankingBenchmark/main.swift`: arguments `--output <dir>` (required), `--configurations <name,...>` (default: all), `--repeats <n>` (default 3). Writes `report.json` and `report.md` to the output folder, and prints the markdown table.
+- `Benchmarks/Sources/RankingBenchmark/Configurations.swift`: the real configurations. Each one except `retrieval-keyword` uses the embedder `PooledEmbedder(ref: "mlx-community/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-4bit-DWQ")`, so the candidates of the decision tier are the same as the retrieval results:
+  - `retrieval-keyword`: no embedder, `.retrieval`.
+  - `retrieval-semantic`: `.retrieval`.
+  - `selection-qwen3-4b`: `.selection`, `SelectionConfig(model: PooledModel(ref: "mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit"), preamble: .librarianDefault)`.
+  - `selection-apple`: `.selection` with `SystemLanguageModel.default`. When the model is not available, the report row gives the reason and no metrics.
+  - `decision-qwen3-4b`: `.decision`, `DecisionConfig(model: PooledDecisionModel(ref: "mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit"))`. The same weights as `selection-qwen3-4b`, so this row compares the method only.
+  - `decision-decider-4b`: `.decision` with `PooledDecisionModel` on `Mapika/decider-4b-GGUF` and `DeciderPromptFormat`, in a `ModelPool` that loads GGUF files (`HubModelLoader(gguf: LlamaCppModelLoader())`).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `swift build --package-path Benchmarks` passes.
+- [ ] `BenchmarkRunner.run` gives one report row for each configuration, with the metrics of each intent kind, p50, p95, the warm-up duration and the error count.
+- [ ] An error in one search does not stop the run.
+- [ ] `RankingBenchmark --output <dir>` writes `report.json` and `report.md` to `<dir>`.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Benchmarks/Tests/BenchmarkSupportTests/BenchmarkRunnerTests.swift`, with no real model: a `retrieval-keyword` configuration, and a `.decision` configuration over a stub `DecisionModel` that gives P(yes) = 1 for the labeled ids. Check that the stub row has hit@1 = 1 for the labeled intents and an empty result for the off-topic intents; that a stub model that throws gives an error count and not a crash; that the warm-up search is not in p50/p95.
+- [ ] `Benchmarks/Tests/BenchmarkSupportTests/ArgumentParsingTests.swift`: the arguments, the defaults, an unknown configuration name, and a missing `--output`. Put the parser in `BenchmarkSupport` so that the test target can reach it.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --package-path Benchmarks`. All tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
